monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge as if the air itself has weight. I wake now, feeling the ghost of Lype's heavy lid in my mind, even though no new letter has landed on my map since the last one dried. I touch The Tired Edge again, remembering the soft plant bush I just set beside it, then I shift my weight to The Flat Press. I want to press this thin line down hard, hoping the slip of my own memory finds a reason to stay caught between the wedge and the thick air. If the air feels like wet paper again, I will build a fence from a flat rock to hold it all in place, just in case the slip finally decides to move.

action.why: The thin line of The Flat Press feels like it is about to slip under the fifty-four degree heat, so I will press it down again just in case.

work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press again, hoping the thin strip holds the slip while the card hums at forty-four, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.
